source: Gyurme Dorje, Tibetan Elemental Divination Paintings, 2001, ill-health printed pp296–305 / PDF297–306

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: ill-health-vs-medical-Blue-Beryl
source_notes.paraphrase: The author distinguishes this elemental divination treatment of illness from medical pulse/urine diagnostics in Sangye Gyatso's Blue Beryl, Part IV. These are not the same medical or predictive procedure.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: nineteen-pebble-serious-illness
source_notes.paraphrase: For serious illness, the source uses sixteen vitality/body contrasts with present year, month, day and hour (each a contrast plus growth/decline reading), with three more markers for calendar day, weekday/planet and lunar mansion/constellation.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: illness-pebble-color-code
source_notes.paraphrase: The method counts maternal and friend relations as white, enemy as black, son as one of each, identity water/earth as white, and identity iron/wood/fire as black. These coding conventions differ by relation and identical-element class.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: eight-calendar-day-goddesses
source_notes.paraphrase: Eight goddess categories cycle across the 30 lunar dates: first six cover four dates apiece and last two cover three each, for exactly thirty. This is source symbolism, not evidence of medical prediction.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: pine-tree-fifteen-main-two-extensions
source_notes.paraphrase: The source refers to fifteen principal starting points for the pine-tree illness divination, while Plate10 fig2 visibly has seventeen numbered columns because two further procedures are added at the end. Do not report seventeen canonical main topics.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: first-spirit-loss-present-year
source_notes.paraphrase: First topic estimates the life-spirit from age-counting forward starting at the present year and comparing four personal elements; the source sometimes substitutes father for child, spouse for woman, brother for male, creating non-natal external inputs.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: second-king-throne-enemy-tiger
source_notes.paraphrase: Second topic starts from a Tiger year whose element is an enemy of the subject's element, counting forward by the subject's age; for wood constitutional type the source names Iron Tiger.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: third-felt-hat-variant
source_notes.paraphrase: Third topic is the felt hat/ancestors and describes counting DOWN from Water or Fire Tiger for wood constitution in the narrative, while Moonbeams's cited verse uses a FORWARD Water Tiger count; these readings must be recorded separately.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: fourth-minister-own-tiger
source_notes.paraphrase: Fourth topic uses a Tiger year having the subject's destiny element, counted forward to age, and refers to ministerial or social advice; wood corresponds to Wood Tiger.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: fifth-lynx-wolf-friendly-tiger
source_notes.paraphrase: Fifth topic counts forward from a friend-element Tiger year for age; for wood constitution the translation gives Earth Tiger, connecting the reading to declining vitality or social support.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: sixth-malevolent-enemy-hare
source_notes.paraphrase: Sixth topic counts backwards from an enemy-element Hare year by age; for wood the example is Iron Hare.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: seventh-ogres-friendly-hare
source_notes.paraphrase: Seventh topic counts forward from a friend-element Hare year by age; wood example Earth Hare; it is a distinct onset point from the enemy Hare sixth topic.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: eighth-wish-tree-identity-hare
source_notes.paraphrase: Eighth topic counts forward from a Hare year identical in element to the subject; wood example Wood Hare; described for children's vitality.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: ninth-treasury-mother-or-son-hare
source_notes.paraphrase: Ninth topic counts from a Hare year in mother or son relation, with Fire Hare shown for wood constitution, and interprets treasury/luck/wealth imagery.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: tenth-heavenly-lifeline-relative-13
source_notes.paraphrase: Tenth topic counts forward from the year THIRTEEN before the present year, according to the subject's age; this is not a fixed sexagenary starting sign.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: eleventh-suspended-lifeline-plus-13
source_notes.paraphrase: Eleventh topic counts backwards from THIRTEEN after the present year according to age; this reverses direction relative to topic ten.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: twelfth-hurricane-son-tiger
source_notes.paraphrase: Twelfth topic counts forward from the subject's son-element Tiger year, example Fire Tiger for wood constitution; it describes reputation/social conflict symbolism.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: thirteenth-gatehouse-mother-monkey
source_notes.paraphrase: Thirteenth topic is the gatehouse: prose counts BACKWARD from the subject's mother-element Monkey year, giving Water Monkey for wood type. Embedded Moonbeams appears to count FORWARD for the same Water Monkey; variant not silently resolved.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: fourteenth-pillow-five-before
source_notes.paraphrase: Fourteenth topic counts forward from the fifth year BEFORE the present year according to age, concerning alleged duration of childhood illness.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: fifteenth-earthly-peg-five-after
source_notes.paraphrase: Fifteenth topic counts BACKWARD from the fifth year AFTER the current year according to subject's age, concerning symbolic life-grid and earthly gate.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: sixteenth-seventeenth-two-school-versions
source_notes.paraphrase: Plate10 fig2 contains two extra columns 16 and 17 attributed to different traditions (Narapa and Dungpa). Both use an impeded starting-point reading but differ in what is contrasted: subject life/body/destiny/luck numeric squares against present year, and present year's life/body/destiny/luck numeric squares. These are alternatives, not two new observed clinical cases.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: four-sets-of-four-conclusive-illness
source_notes.paraphrase: Across each selected pine-tree starting point, sixteen pebbles correspond to the subject's vitality, body, destiny and luck crossed with the reference set. Mostly white/all white are read favorably; mixed or majority black and all-black have different interpretations.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: seven-great-three-family-sectors
source_notes.paraphrase: Seven illustrative diagnostic schemes partition three five-marker sectors as male, female and child, alongside symbolic comparisons of household, ancestors and livestock. It is not solely the subject's physiology.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: bridge-juniper-fruit-household-charts
source_notes.paraphrase: Within the seven greater divinations, golden bridges, juniper branches, wish-granting fruit and fortunate/unfortunate household signs depend on number/location of linked white or broken black pebble connections; the target can be spouse, child or household.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: living-dying-eye-published-errors
source_notes.paraphrase: The living/dying-eye chart uses four outer points and one central opposite-colored point, with different results when black versus white disappears. The commentator explicitly flags incorrectly colored central dots in the illustrated plate, so the literal table must not be silently trusted.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: disease-demon-four-input-layers
source_notes.paraphrase: Recognition of illnesses and demons is described using log-men year, natal/current trigram, weekday and mewa, with source passages assigning contrasting remedies/omens. These are cultural causal claims, not clinical evidence.

anchor.source_section: White Beryl ill-health pp296–305; relevant White Beryl ff.274b–299a, Moonbeams ff.31b–33b

source_notes.title: five-year-month-day-hour-diagnostic-count
source_notes.paraphrase: The so-called actual disease-recognition calculation uses five pebbles: four from current year, month, day and hour elements plus one representing their majority element, and an associated trigram from month. Exact elemental-composition categories are named but not medically validated.

source_issues: PDF299 Plate10 fig2 displays fifteen main entries plus 16/17 variants; exact relation to narrative 15 topics preserved.
PDF298 item three narrative downwards with Water/Fire Tiger vs Moonbeams PDF300 forwards Water Tiger.
PDF298 item thirteen backwards Water Monkey vs Moonbeams PDF300 forwards Water Monkey.
PDF302 text explicitly identifies published colored-dot errors in the living/dying-eye figure.
source_limits: Medical-sounding outcomes, death, disease causes and suggested rituals are never used as medical advice. No patient outcome measurements, no supervised assessment or verified efficacy.
